comments.body:
I traced this to the already-ready fast path in `futureImpl.Chain`.

When the source future is already ready, `Chain` currently copies `value`, `err` and `ready=true` directly onto the destination future but it does not complete the destination via `Set(...)`.

That leaves the destination future in a partially completed state:

* `Get()` can still block because the internal channel is never closed
* chained dependents are not propagated since that happens in `Set()`

The fix is to route the already-ready path through the normal completion logic:

```go
val, err := ch.GetValueAndError()
f.Set(val, err)
```

I’m validating this with regression tests for both the direct `Get()` hang and transitive chained propagation.

title: futureImpl.Chain blocks Get forever when called with an already-ready Future
